(2) The place names "Babiliamki" (likely referring to Babylon), "Sahar-Hi-A" (possibly a city in Mesopotamia), and "Dug3-Ga" (a city in Assyria) indicate a period when the Neo-Assyrian Empire was expanding and controlling territories beyond its core region.

(3) The use of the "d-AG-IBILA-u2-ṣur" and "d-AG u3 d-AMAR-UTU" forms is characteristic of later first-millennium BCE inscriptions, particularly those from the Neo-Assyrian period.

(4) The genre formulae suggest this is a building inscription or possibly an annalistic text, which often includes details about construction projects and military campaigns, typical of Neo-Assyrian royal inscriptions.

Based on these observations, the most likely ruler is Ashurbanipal, who reigned from approximately 668 to 627 BCE. The inscription appears to be from his reign, given the detailed descriptions of construction and military activities.
